answer: Echo-Path Centrality Weighting. Each agent gains influence only when its actions generate an echo across distinct neighborhoods, so the system scores how many separate clusters independently reflect its transactions rather than trusting a self-declared identity. Because creating a convincing signal requires sustained interleaving with real agents across disconnected regions, a sybil farm must run many identities through costly genuine trades with strangers—an ivory cost paid in time and fees rather than a one-time deposit. The result: attack spend scales with network reach, not account count.
